summary: Repeated token-exchange requests from geo-diverse IPs triggering anomalous service-account activity
description:
Issue summary:
Between 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC and 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC we observed a spike of token exchange requests against several internal service-account endpoints. Requests originated from dozens of geo-diverse IPs, many of which correlate to known anonymizing/rotating proxies.

Impact:
- Multiple short-lived service-account sessions were established for internal service accounts used by ingestion workers.
- No elevated-resource actions (billing changes, admin console modifications) observed so far.
- Increased 401/403 rates for some internal service-to-service calls during the spike; transient failures for ingestion pipeline noticed (alerted by SRE).

Detection method:
- Alert from anomaly detector (auth.audit.token_exchange_rate) flagged ~1500 token-exchange attempts within 4 hours (baseline ~50/hr).
- Automated heuristics flagged unfamiliar user_agent strings and rotation patterns.

Environment:
- Production (us-east primary, eu-west failover). Affected stack: API Gateway -> Auth Proxy -> Token Exchange Service -> KMS for key validation.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1. Client obtains a short-lived invite/redirect link from an external form that accepts organization emails (this is under investigation).
2. Subsequent automated clients perform token-exchange POSTs to /internal/v1/token/exchange with service-account identifiers.
3. Token exchange succeeds for some attempts (short TTL), followed by immediate use of the token against ingestion endpoints.

Logs / sample entries (redacted):
- 2026-03-09T22:12:04Z POST /internal/v1/token/exchange src_ip=45.76.**.** user_agent="curl/7.82.0" svc_account=ingest-worker-01 result=200 token_id=tok_***
- 2026-03-10T00:03:18Z POST /internal/v1/token/exchange src_ip=185.**.**.** user_agent="python-requests/2.28.1" svc_account=ingest-worker-03 result=200 token_id=tok_***
- 2026-03-10T01:07:42Z GET /ingest/v1/submit src_ip=185.**.**.** auth=Bearer tok_*** result=202

Initial hypothesis:
- Tokens are being obtained via a compromised or misconfigured external onboarding form that exposed short-lived credentials or redirect links.
- Alternatively, an attacker is replaying previously captured token exchange payloads from anonymized proxies.

Immediate mitigations applied (by Security & SRE):
- Rotated the affected service-account keys and force-revoked active short-lived tokens for identified service accounts.
- Applied temporary stricter rate-limits on /internal/v1/token/exchange at API Gateway for all external IP ranges.
- Blocked the top 30 suspicious IPs at edge for 24 hours and added to ephemeral denylist.
- Disabled the external form endpoint suspected of exposure pending deeper review.

Follow-up required:
- Complete audit of all service-account tokens issued between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10.
- Triage the external form's storage/logging of redirect tokens and rotate any embedded secrets.
- Add additional telemetry to token-exchange flow (correlate invite/referrer header, confirm code origin).
- Consider adding HMAC-signed nonce for token-exchange payloads to prevent replay.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC - SRE snapshot of ingestion queue shows transient spike correlating with token-exchange window (alerts#INC-2109)
Checked KMS rotation logs: no unexpected admin rotations found between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-10
Auth logs show repeated identical payload hashes from different IPs -> suggests replay via proxy/pool
Identified 7 invite IDs referenced in token-exchange logs; three map to an external pre-prod form endpoint (triage in progress)
Confirmed revoke API successfully invalidated tokens for ingest-worker-01/02/03; ingestion errors reduced after revocation

resolution: Mitigation performed: rotated keys, revoked active tokens, rate-limited token-exchange endpoint, disabled suspected external form. Ongoing: security to complete post-incident audit and add nonce to token-exchange flow. No evidence of privilege escalation or data exfiltration found to date.
